paper.title: Measuring Scalar Constructs in Social Science with LLMs
paper.authors: Licht, Sarkar, Wu, Goel, Stoehr, Ash, Hoyle

source.licence: None stated: the release repo has no LICENSE file and the README grants no terms. Underlying data: Carlson & Montgomery (2017, APSR) replication data (survey responses; WiscAds 2008 storyboards, which the Wisconsin Advertising Project distributes under its own academic-use terms) and Park (2021, JOP) hearing paragraphs. Texts are therefore NOT copied into data/frozen: only item IDs, text SHA-256s, gold BT scores, pair IDs and pair labels are frozen; items() rebuilds texts from data/raw and verifies each hash.
source.gold: bt_scores.jsonl `label` = Bradley-Terry score of each text fit with choix ILSR (alpha 1e-4, max_iter 1000) to all human comparisons in data.jsonl (release src/bt.py). Our numpy/scipy port of ilsr_pairwise_dense reproduces the released scores from data.jsonl (see validation). Pair label 1/2 = which text the (single) crowd annotator chose; no ties in any test split.

frozen.builder: scripts/prepare_scalar_constructs.py (downloads 48 release files, verifies SHA-256 against data/frozen/scalar_constructs/raw_sha256.json, writes the freeze; re-run is byte-identical)
frozen.layout: per construct: items.jsonl {id, sha256 (UTF-8 text), bt_score} in bt_scores.jsonl order for every text in any fold's test pairs; pairs.jsonl {fold, pair_id, id1, id2, label} per fold in release file order; folds.json per fold {n_pairs, test_item_ids (test-pair items minus train-pair items: the release notebook's evaluation set), heldout_item_ids (additionally minus val-pair items: the paper's V_test, 100)}
frozen.sent_to_jev: pointwise: the text as a JSON string state; pairwise: the release's formatted pair string (byte-identical to prompting/pairwise_comparison/data/<dataset>/0.test.pairwise.expanded.jsonl) as a JSON string state. BT scores, labels, IDs and expert ratings are never sent.

test_n_resolution.note: Test set = fold 0 of the released graph splits (seed 112358, 100 high-degree held-out vertices), which is the only fold the paper's prompting experiments (Table 2) use. Pairwise tasks: every fold-0 test pair (3,265 / 1,944 / 2,228). Pointwise tasks: every text in the test pairs of any of the 5 folds (334 / 935 / 3,414), so that fold 0 (primary) and the 5-fold protocol of Table 3 (supplementary) can both be scored; fold 0 alone needs 334 / 855 / 1,673 texts. Rho/RMSE are computed over the release notebook's 'test items' = items in test pairs minus items in train pairs = 100 / 151 / 303 (the 51 and 203 extra ad and hearing texts are train-graph vertices whose edges all landed in the val split); the strict 100-vertex V_test variant is reported alongside. Paper Table 1 counts 6,489 / 9,489 / 38,348 pairs; the release data.jsonl has 6,640 / 9,528 / 38,500 annotation rows = 6,281 / 9,431 / 38,179 distinct item pairs (graph edges; the splits keep one row per edge, the last one in file order). Text counts 334 / 935 / 3,499 match Table 1.

english_verification.metadata: Paper Limitations: 'our datasets only include English-language texts with applications focused on U.S. politics'. Sources: U.S. survey responses, U.S. Senate TV ad storyboards, U.S. House hearing transcripts.
english_verification.method: langid 1.1.6 (all languages) over all 4,768 released texts (334 + 935 + 3,499), plus a non-Latin-letter count, a >5% non-ASCII ratio check, and a Spanish function-word scan (>= 3 hits); every flag inspected.
english_verification.result: 15 langid flags, all Immigration Fear keyword-style English answers (e.g. items 10470, 10602, 10360, 10503). No non-Latin letters and no non-ASCII-heavy texts in any dataset. The Spanish scan hit one English ad (ad_negativity item 7507, where 'con' is an English word). No non-English or code-mixed rows; nothing dropped.

primitives.pointwise: score, 9 levels (1-9 as in the paper, 'We use a range between 1 and 9', Section 3.2); one request per text; prediction = sum_s P(s)*s / sum_s P(s) (paper Eq. 1) from Jev's level probabilities. Supplementary: modal level (paper's 'naive').
primitives.pairwise: choice {'1','2'}; four requests per pair = the paper's augmentations (App. A.2 / Table 5: label swap x order reversal); P(text1 wins) = mean of the four aligned probabilities (release debias_pairwise_locally); choice 1 / 2 / tie at exactly 0.5; item scores = BT fit (ported choix ILSR, alpha 1e-4, max_iter 1000) to the predicted choices on the fold-0 test pairs. Supplementary: no debiasing (original presentation only, release default_output).

metrics.primary: Spearman rho between predicted item scores and gold BT scores over the fold-0 test items (paper Section 3.3: 'Our primary focus is on LLMs' scoring performance'); headline value = mean over 25 bootstrap resamples (np.random.RandomState(42), notebook row order), exactly as Table 2 reports.
metrics.also: RMSE after min-max rescaling both score vectors to [0,1] over the test items; pairwise accuracy over all fold-0 test pairs (a predicted tie counts as wrong); accuracy on test-test pairs; point estimates; V_test-only variant; pointwise 5-fold mean +- sd of point estimates (Table 3 protocol).
metrics.implementation: ported from release prompting/evaluate_prompting.ipynb (get_itemwise_results / get_pairwise_results), src/icl/evaluation.py, src/icl/debias.py, src/bt.py; verified by replaying the paper's released model outputs (see validation).

truncation: Frozen rule: each text cut to its first 20,000 characters; the longest text has 2,288 characters, so n_truncated = 0 for all tasks.
deviations: Zero-shot only: Jev is compared with the paper's 0-shot prompting rows; 5-shot rows and fine-tuned models are reported as reference points.
Pointwise tasks additionally score texts from folds 1-4 (334 / 935 / 3,414 texts instead of 334 / 855 / 1,673) to report the Table 3 5-fold protocol; the fold-0 primary numbers use fold-0 texts only.

Prompt adaptation: the release's zero-shot prompt is sent verbatim as the question instructions, except the {text} slot (replaced by a note that the text is the state) and the final '**Response**: [Output only ...]' line (dropped; the primitive fixes the answer space).

Pairwise state strings are byte-identical to the release's expanded pair files; the Immigration Fear file quotes the labels ('"**Text 1**": ...') and names the two mixed augmentations the other way round (_0_1 <-> _1_0) relative to the committed format_text_pair; the four presented strings per pair are identical, and the debiasing average is unaffected.

Evaluation item set follows the release notebook (test-pair items minus train-pair items: 100 / 151 / 303), which is what Table 2 reports, not the 100 V_test vertices described in Section 3.3; the V_test-only numbers are reported as a supplement.
Jev's probabilities replace the paper's next-token probabilities over '1'-'9' / '1','2' (the paper renormalises over the scale tokens; Jev's level probabilities already sum to 1).

validation.offline_only: No Jev calls. All checks below were run on 2026-09-26 against the frozen data.

requests.checks: every request JSON-serialisable; request hashes unique within each task (34,431 distinct); largest request ~1.7K tokens, far below 32K

validation.pair_strings: all 29,748 pairwise states are byte-identical to the `text` field of the release's 0.test.pairwise.expanded.jsonl files (Immigration Fear with the _0_1/_1_0 naming swap).
validation.bradley_terry_port: bt_fit on the release data.jsonl reproduces bt_scores.jsonl to max |diff| 5.0e-11 for all three datasets.
validation.table2_replay: The paper's released LLM outputs (prompting/{absolute_scoring,pairwise_comparison}/outputs, 5 models x {0,5}-shot x {pointwise,pairwise} x 3 datasets = 60 configurations) fed through predict() + the fold-0 scorer reproduce every Table 2 accuracy / rho / RMSE value to the printed 2 decimals (max deviation 0.01 on half-way rounding cases). E.g. Qwen-2.5-72B pointwise 0-shot Immigration Fear: paper .76/.81/.23, replay .763/.815/.233; pairwise 0-shot Grandstanding: paper .66/.48/.20, replay .657/.483/.202.
validation.table3_replay: The released fine-tuned reward-model predictions (finetuning/outputs/pairwise) through the 5-fold scorer reproduce Table 3, e.g. DeBERTa-v3-large (all) Immigration Fear paper .78/.91/.18, replay .780/.911/.178 (sd .002/.020/.040); Grandstanding paper .68/.78/.16, replay .676/.777/.158.

gold_derived_oracles.note: Pointwise accuracy ceilings (.83/.85/.73) are the agreement of the gold BT scores with the single human labels of the test pairs. The pairwise rho ceilings are below 1 because the BT fit sees only the fold-0 test pairs (the gold uses all pairs); the Grandstanding ceiling (.63) bounds any pairwise judge on this protocol.
gold_derived_oracles.ties: all-0.5 answers give choice 0 (tie, counted wrong), matching the release's margin-0 rule

validation.runtime_note: score() fits BT with dense LU on up to 1,673 items; ~7 s for all six oracle scorings with 4 BLAS threads, but minutes under heavy BLAS oversubscription (set OMP_NUM_THREADS/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS on a loaded machine).
